root_cause: src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/transformations/batch_replicated_branches.cpp uses single-statement if/for bodies without braces (lines 123, 148, 156, 162, 176, 189, 206, 227, 245, 284). The clang-tidy 18 job runs with -Werror and the readability-braces-around-statements check enabled, so these 10 brace-less statements are reported as errors and abort the ninja build. This file is pre-existing in the GPU plugin and is entirely unrelated to the files changed by PR #39853 (ONNX frontend BitShift translator); the merge-queue run simply surfaces this latent, already-recurring clang-tidy violation whenever the GPU clang-tidy job runs against current master content.
reproduction_steps: Build the intel_gpu plugin with clang-tidy enabled: `cmake -DENABLE_CLANG_TIDY=ON ... && ninja openvino_intel_gpu_plugin`, or directly run `clang-tidy-18 --extra-arg-before=--driver-mode=g++ src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/transformations/batch_replicated_branches.cpp -- <same compile flags as in the failed job log>` and observe the readability-braces-around-statements errors at the listed line numbers.
recommended_actions: Add braces around the single-statement bodies at the flagged lines (123, 148, 156, 162, 176, 189, 206, 227, 245, 284) in src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/transformations/batch_replicated_branches.cpp
Run clang-tidy locally with the readability-braces-around-statements check before merging GPU plugin changes that touch this file
Consider a repo-wide clang-format/clang-tidy auto-fix pass for this pre-existing violation so it stops recurring on every unrelated merge-queue run
prevention_strategies: Enable clang-tidy as a pre-commit or local CI gate for intel_gpu plugin changes so brace-around-statements violations are caught before merge; alternatively run `clang-tidy --fix` on this file once to close out the backlog so it stops failing merge-queue runs for unrelated PRs.
historical_context: This exact signature (a4282c65071120e2) has now recurred 4 times within ~5 hours (06:08, 08:31, 10:56, and this run), affecting unrelated PRs #38575, #38641, and now #39853 — confirming it is a long-standing, unfixed code-quality issue in batch_replicated_branches.cpp rather than something introduced by any of the affected PRs.
